chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Knowledge is of two kinds: absorbed (internalized) and heard (external). The heard does not benefit unless it is absorbed.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between absorbed and heard knowledge in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between 'masmūʿ' (knowledge acquired through hearing or external study) and 'maṭbūʿ' (knowledge deeply internalized and engraved in the soul). He asserts that the former is ineffective without the latter, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the transformation of knowledge into character and spiritual insight rather than mere intellectual accumulation. This distinction underscores the necessity of contemplation (tafakkur) and practice (ʿamal) to convert information into true wisdom (ḥikmah).

en.sayed-ali-raza: 338. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Knowledge is of two kinds — that which is absorbed and that which is just heard. The one that is heard does not give benefit unless it is absorbed.
